title: Add contextual metric merge and SILK alert scheduler
author: Miguel Ortega
release_notes: Introduces a contextual metric-merge stage to reduce cardinality noise and a SILK alert scheduler that adapts alert windows to invocation burstiness and tail variance. Defaults off behind feature flag; opt-in recommended for large tenants.
commits: d3f2b1c Add contextual metric signature generator and merge pipeline
a7b4e89 Implement SILK scheduler and window-adaptation policy
c1e3a55 Add unit tests for merge heuristics and scheduler math
b9f8d77 Add integration/e2e bench that replays production token-bursts
f44c2a0 Docs: observability guide + feature-flag config examples
description:
Context and motivation:
High-cardinality metric series and short-lived token bursts have been driving a large fraction of noisy SLO alerts (see ENG-4621). Transactional features with ephemeral context keys produce many near-duplicate metric series that differ only in minor labels; downstream alerting treats them separately which inflates both alert volume and mean time to triage. Separately, fixed alert windows do not adapt well to bursty token patterns: short bursts of tail latency cause repeated transient alerts.

What this PR does (single-string summary):
- Introduces a lightweight contextual metric merge stage that groups metric series based on a stable signature (prefix+selective labels+hash of normalized context). The merge is deterministic and reversible for debugging: we keep the original labels as an annotation so operators can expand a merged series back to its constituents.
- Adds the SILK (Sampler-Interval-Latency-Kalibrator) alert scheduler that dynamically adjusts SLO evaluation windows per-route based on observed tail variance, token-burst score, and recent merge cardinality. SILK reduces sensitivity to microbursts while preserving responsiveness for sustained regressions.
- Opt-in feature-flag (observability.feature_flags.contextual_merge = true) and per-tenant throttles with safe defaults.
- Adds unit, integration and an e2e replay bench that compares alert rate/precision between baseline and SILK-enabled mode.

Key design decisions and tradeoffs:
- Merge heuristics favor recall over precision at the ingest layer (we prefer to collapse noisy duplicates rather than create false negatives). To mitigate the risk of masking true regressions, merged series carry provenance annotations and a sampling mechanism that keeps a small fraction of originals unmerged for fidelity checks.
- SILK uses a two-tier windowing policy: a fast detection band for sustained increases and a slow band that suppresses repeat alerts during short high-variance bursts. Tunables exposed in config for enterprise customers.
- Computational cost: the signature generator is O(1) per metric with an extra ~1% CPU on the ingest path in our bench (see results). We added a sharded LRU to limit memory for signature interning.

Checklist:
- [x] Contextual signature + merge implementation
- [x] SILK scheduler and adaptive window algorithm
- [x] Unit tests for merge heuristics and scheduler math
- [x] Integration test that verifies provenance annotations and expansion API
- [x] E2E replay bench and comparison script
- [x] Docs and config examples
- [x] Feature flag gating + helm values

Benchmarks (local replay vs production-like traces):
- Baseline alert volume: 1,100 alerts/day across sampled tenants
- SILK + contextual merge: 620 alerts/day (-44%) in default tuning
- Precision (hand-labeled sample): baseline 72% -> SILK 86%
- Ingest CPU overhead: +0.9% median; peak +1.8% during floods
- Memory: signature cache added ~120MB across 10 shard instances on our bench cluster

Commits summary (what to review):
- metric_merge.py/pkg/merge_signature.go: core signature functions, normalization rules, provenance annotation format. Pay attention to label selection heuristics (comments inline).
- silk_scheduler.py: adaptive window math (alpha/beta knobs), burst detector implementation, and the scheduler loop. The algorithm is documented in the header.
- tests: unit coverage added for corner cases (high-cardinality churn, late-arriving label changes).
- docs: operational guide with examples for tuning per-tenant.

Review conversation highlights:
- Sophie Liu: requested explicit config name changes and an escape hatch to force no-merge by label. Implemented and added docs (see commit f44c2a0).
- Ravi Menon: asked for stronger guarantees on provenance expansion API; added integration test and an API-level endpoint that returns expansion samples.
- Elena Park: flagged potential flakiness in the e2e bench (timing-dependent); we added jitter stabilization and reran the bench.
- Author replies: added tests, clarified comments in signature heuristics, and tuned default SILK thresholds after bench feedback.

CI and validation:
- CI initially failed with a flakey bench test (timeout) in the first run; rerun cleared the issue. All unit and integration checks are green. Static analysis linter flagged two minor export name issues which were fixed.

Operational notes and rollout plan:
- Feature is behind observability.feature_flags.contextual_merge. Default for hosted customers is OFF for the next two weeks; internal tenants can opt-in.
- Gradual rollout: enable for 5 small tenants -> monitor precision/recall drift and CPU/memory -> 25% traffic -> full.
- Monitoring to add before rollout: merged_series_count, merge_collision_rate, silk_suppressed_alerts, silk_window_adjustments. Dashboards added under observability/dashboard/token-burst-inspector.json.
- Rollback: flip feature flag and purge signature cache per-shard (script included in infra/helm).

Follow-ups and TODOs:
- Add a lightweight offline trainer to recommend SILK thresholds per-tenant based on 7d history (ENG-4702).
- Add sampling-based periodic expansion tests in prod to validate no regression masking.
- Explore an automatic revert policy if suppressed-alerts spike beyond threshold.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers (Sophie Liu, Ravi Menon, Elena Park).
- Squash-merged to main on 2025-11-20.

If you're reviewing, focus on: signature normalization edge cases (observability/ingest/metric_merge.py), scheduler math invariants (observability/schedulers/silk_scheduler.py), and the e2e replay bench config (examples/bench/replay-burst-workload.py).
